mainEntity.name: How does a pre-engineered metal home differ from a residential pole barn or barndominium?

acceptedAnswer.text: A pre-engineered metal home uses rigid red-iron I-beams or heavy-gauge steel framing bolted directly to an engineered concrete foundation, whereas a pole barn home relies on wood posts buried in the ground. Pole barns (post-frame buildings) have shorter lifespans due to subterranean wood rot and foundation shifting over time. Pre-engineered steel buildings are designed under commercial-grade residential structural codes, offering superior structural longevity, higher wind resistance ratings, and greater stability for permanent, multi-generational living without risk of sagging or pest infestation.
